papers.title: Microbial Metabolites Short-Chain Fatty Acids (Scfas) In Implant Osseointegration
papers.abstract: To investigate the effect of antibiotic-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis on implant osseointegration and the role of microbial metabolites short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in implant osseointegration. 4-week-old male SPF C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into four groups: SPF group (normal water), antibiotics treated (AbT) group (broad-spectrum antibiotics water), microbiota recolonization group (Co-house), and SCFAs group (broad-spectrum antibiotics + SCFAs water). The bacterial DNA was extracted from mouse feces, and the bacterial content was detected via RT PCR. SCFAs concentrations in serum were measured via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Implants were inserted into the femur of mice, and micro-CT and methylene blue stained sections were used to evaluate the osseointegration after 4 weeks. AbT group exhibited a significant reduction in bacterial content, while no significant difference was observed between SPF group and Co-house group. Compared with SPF group, bone volume fraction (BV/TV), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th), and bone-implant contact (BIC) of mice in AbT group were significantly reduced, and trabecular separation (Tb.Sp) was significantly increased, while no significant difference was found between Co-house group and SPF group, indicating impaired osseointegration in AbT group. Following oral supplementation with SCFAs, there was a notable increase in BV/TV and BIC, as well as a significant decrease in Tb.Sp, suggesting substantial improvement in osseointegration. Gut microbiota dysbiosis could cause impaired implant osseointegration. Supplementation of SCFAs was able to restore the implant osseointegration.

papers.title: Rotary Transcrestal Sinus Floor Elevation With Simultaneous Implant Placement
papers.abstract: To evaluate the clinical and radiographic outcomes of rotary transcrestal sinus floor elevation without bone grafting with simultaneous implant placement. Twenty-nine patients received 32 implants with simultaneous rotary transcrestal sinus floor elevation(rotary technique). The rotary technique was performed concurrently with implant osteotomy preparation. First, a pilot drill was used to create the initial osteotomy and to perforate the cortical bone of the sinus floor with scrupulous attention to detail. Subsequently, step drills are employed to widen the implant bed and the sinus floor. Finally, the implant apex loaded with autologous concentrated growth factors (CGF) was advanced to achieve concurrent membrane elevation and implant placement. Parameters evaluated included the frequency of intraoperative Schneiderian membrane perforation and postoperative swelling, vertical bone gain in the sinus and implant survival rates. All implant sites achieved osseointegration with favorable prosthetic rehabilitation. Radiographic evaluation demonstrated significant new bone formation around implants, exhibiting a mean height of endo-sinus bone gain(5.05±1.09 mm). Without using osteotome and mallet, this technique significantly reduced intraoperative discomfort and postoperative swelling incidence. The Schneiderian membrane perforation rate remained at 3.1%(1/32), while implants survival maintained at 100% during follow-up. The rotary technique lifts the sinus and places the implant in one step using gentle drilling. It’s less invasive, more comfortable during the procedure, and reduces the postoperative morbidity. Despite the limitations of the present study, it seems that the rotary technique can achieve satisfactory therapeutic effect and high success rate.

papers.title: Modified Immediate Dentoalveolar Restoration (IDR) Technique For Peri-Implantitis Management
papers.abstract: A 41-year-old female patient presented with complaints of recurrent fistula formation in the area of a previously placed implant in position 21. Clinical and radiographic evaluation, including cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), revealed peri-implantitis with significant loss of the buccal bone wall. Given the esthetic demands of the case and the severity of the defect, a modified technique of Immediate Dentoalveolar Restoration (IDR) was selected. The IDR technique involves simultaneous implant placement, bone augmentation, and provisional restoration, ensuring both functional and esthetic rehabilitation. The protocol was modified by incorporating flap elevation in the surgical field. Stage 1: The previously placed implant in position 21 was removed. A new implant was immediately inserted into the site, followed by bone augmentation using the modified IDR technique. A provisional crown was placed to achieve immediate functional and esthetic outcomes. Stage 2: After six months, the provisional restoration was replaced with a definitive prosthesis. Adjacent teeth were restored with ceramic veneers/crowns to further enhance esthetics. The modified IDR technique resulted in successful implant placement in the peri-implantitis-affected site. Postoperative follow-up demonstrated excellent osseointegration, substantial bone regeneration, and soft tissue adaptation. This case highlights the efficacy and efficiency of the modified IDR technique for managing peri-implantitis in the esthetic zone. The combination of immediate implant placement with simultaneous bone augmentation ensured optimal restoration of both function and esthetics. The modification involving flap elevation proved advantageous in managing extensive defects, supporting successful outcomes in challenging clinical scenarios.

papers.title: The Application Of Socket Shield Technique In The Aesthetic Zone
papers.abstract: After tooth extraction, ridge dimensional changes are inevitable, leading to unfavorable and irreversible shrinkage, particularly in aesthetic areas. Socket shield technique mitigates vestibular volume loss by preserving a root fragment attached to the periodontal ligament, which helps maintain the bundle bone. Animal studies show that retaining such fragments significantly reduces post-extraction volume loss. A 38-year-old female presented with a fractured crown on tooth #23. Clinical examination revealed a residual root with a subgingival fracture and no inflammation. CBCT demonstrated a subosseous root fracture (6.7 mm), leaving only 5.6 mm of intact intra-alveolar root length, a thin labial bone wall (0.9 mm), and apical bone loss. The patient had a thin gingival biotype and a 5.2 mm contact point-to-crest distance. To preserve labial bone and soft tissue aesthetics, the socket shield technique was selected for immediate implant placement. The socket shield technique demonstrates significant versatility through its adaptable design parameters, allowing clinicians to tailor treatment according to specific anatomical and prosthetic requirements. But it requires exacting precision in both root fragment preparation and implant placement. Meticulous contouring of the tooth fragment is essential to avoid complications, particularly given the documented risks of osseointegration failure and shield displacement associated with direct implant-to-shield contact. The socket shield technique offers certain advantages in preserving the contour of labial soft and hard tissues and enhancing aesthetic restoration outcomes.

papers.title: Preserving Peri-Implant Tissue Architecture With Immediate Implant Placement
papers.abstract: Immediate implantation in a fresh extraction socket is a technically demanding procedure that requires manual skill for precise execution. However, when performed correctly, it helps preserve the bone and soft tissues surrounding the implant. We will present a case involving dental implantation in the frontal area of the maxilla, specifically replacing the central incisor immediately. During the same session, a provisional restoration was created using the natural crown of a previously extracted tooth. After the osseointegration period, we proceeded to the final prosthodontic stage, which involved taking digital impressions at the implant level and producing a custom abutment to retain a full ceramic crown. Immediate implantation is a scientifically supported procedure that allows for the replacement of a tooth right after it is extracted. This approach significantly reduces the time needed for restoration and helps maintain the natural contours of the surrounding soft and hard tissues around the implant. Often, immediate implantation is performed simultaneously with soft tissue and bone augmentation, which enhance the thickness of the tissues. This combination contributes to achieving both aesthetic appeal and lasting results. Our case demonstrates the benefits of immediate implantation and provisionalization. After four months of osseointegration, the implant reached secondary stability and provided satisfactory aesthetic results in the final stage.

papers.title: Implant Therapy After Taking Antiresorptive Drugs:A Case Report
papers.abstract: Antiresorptive drugs (ARDs) are commonly used in the treatment of osteoporosis and may cause drug-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ). The implantologist has to deal with the side effects of drugs in implant therapy and to take appropriate prognostic measures. A 24-year-old female presented to restore a missing tooth and who had been treated with the antiresorptive drug Desutumab for osteoporosis 2 months previously. After routine implanting procedures, intravenous antibiotics were administered 5 days to prevent postoperative infection. The CBCT results showed that the initial stability was poor, with more marginal bone resorption, and it was decided to extend the healing time, and the patient was instructed to take calcium tablets. After 8 months of postoperative follow-up, the patient was found to have good osseointegration, a healing abutment was placed, and a two-stage crown restoration was performed. The use of ARDs may have an impact on bone remodelling, but patients treated with low-dose short-term therapy have a good short-term prognosis and only exhibit poor initial stability, which can be treated aggressively with anti-infective therapy along with load reduction to promote osseointegration. However, the implantologist should remain vigilant in patients treated at high or low doses for long periods of time and use other restorative techniques if necessary. The prognosis for dental implant is favourable in patients treated with low-dose osteoporosis medication. However, long-term stability needs to be monitored.

papers.title: Integrated Management Of Implant Apical Infection And Adjacent Lesions
papers.abstract: Introduction Implant apical infections may spread to adjacent teeth, requiring multidisciplinary intervention. This case demonstrates the retention of an infected implant (31) with concurrent periapical lesions in tooth 32 through combined surgical and endodontic approaches. Case description A 55-year-old male developed swelling and purulent discharge at implant 31 three months post-placement using bone condensation (initial bone width <5 mm). CBCT revealed vertical bone loss (>3 mm) at the implant apex, reduced bone density, and periapical radiolucency at tooth 32. Treatment included: Stage 1: Apical flap debridement with EDTA gel biofilm removal, minocycline local delivery, and Bio-Oss/collagen membrane bone regeneration. Stage 2: Microscopic root canal therapy on tooth 32. Successful osseointegration occurred at six months, followed by zirconia crown restoration with light occlusal contact. Discussion Key pathological mechanisms: Bidirectional infection: Implant apical pathogens spread via trabecular bone to tooth 32 apex, forming a cross-contamination cycle; Surgical risks: Bone condensation-induced microfractures and thermal injury during osteotomy exacerbated bone resorption and pathogen colonization. Innovative strategies: Targeted apical therapy: Direct debridement of deep implant apicitis using EDTA/minocycline instead of superficial cleaning; Staged bone grafting: Delayed grafting post-infection control minimized graft contamination and addressed bone condensation/thermal damage. Conclusion/clinical significance This protocol establishes a multidisciplinary framework for managing implant-related apical complications: Dual-pathway infection control (implant debridement and root canal therapy) prevents cross-contamination. Sequential bone grafting minimizes inflammatory interference. Emphasizes preventive measures (low-speed drilling, intermittent irrigation) to avoid thermal damage.

papers.title: Thread Design Optimization Of A Dental Implant
papers.abstract: Aim or purpose To optimize the thread design from a commercial dental implant for ideal stress distribution in the surrounding bone. Materials and methods The models of BLT® Φ4.1×10 implant (Institut Straumann AG) and alveolar bone were created. Dynamic von Mises stress (σvM) in the cortical bone during and immediately after implantation was calculated using explicit dynamics finite element analysis (EDFEA). The combination of thread pitch, depth, tip width (TW), and coronal/apical surface angle (CSA/ASA) which produced minimal σvM was determined as the optimal thread design. The implants with optimal and original thread designs were fabricated and implanted into rabbits’ tibias. Implant stability quotient (ISQ), bone-to-implant contact (BIC), and bone volume fraction in 500μm (BV/TV500) and 1000μm range (BV/TV1000) were measured to evaluate the osseointegration performance of the implants. Results The implant thread design of 0.8mm pitch, 0.2mm depth, 0.15mm TW, and 10° CSA/ASA, and 1.0mm pitch, 0.3mm depth, 0.2mm TW, zero CSA, and 20° ASA produced minimal σvM for the maxillary (OPTmax) and mandibular posterior region (OPTman), respectively. Optimized implants showed significantly improved ISQ value 4 weeks after implantation. The BV/TV500 and BV/TV1000 around the OPTmax, and the BIC and BV/TV500 around the OPTman implant were significantly higher than that around the original-designed implant, respectively. Conclusions The thread design significantly affects the stress in the surrounding bone during and immediately after the implantation. The optimal thread design based on EDFEA promoted the osteogenesis around the implant.

papers.title: Bone Healing Of 3D Printing Titanium Implant Combined With Mao
papers.abstract: To investigate the bone healing effect of micro arc oxidation(MAO)coating on 3D printing personalized titanium implants in vivo. The three-dimensional model of the target tooth root was obtained based on CT imaging technology. The individualized titanium implant with the same shape as the root was constructed by using computer aided design (CAD). The implant wasmanufactured by 3D printing with electron beam melting technology. The micro arc oxidation coating was prepared on the surface of the personalized titanium implant, the bilateral mandibular premolars of beagle dogs were extracted, and the personalized implant was immediately implanted. The osseointegration of implants was observed after operation. Compared with the uncoated group, the surface of the implants in the MAO group was rougher and the element content was more abundant. X-ray and hard tissue sections showed that compared with the uncoated group, the bone around the implant in the micro arc oxidation group was more abundant and more closely combined with the surrounding bone. The electron beam melting 3D printing technology can produce titanium implants that are completely consistent with the target tooth shape. The micro arc oxidation coating can better promote the bone bonding of 3D printed porous personalized titanium implants.

papers.title: Micro-Arc Oxidized Titanium-Cerium Alloy Enhances Osseointegration Under Osteoporosis
papers.abstract: To address the issue of poor bone-implant combination ratio (BIC%) among osteoporotic patients, this study aimed to develop a micro-arc oxidized titanium-cerium alloy and investigate its regulatory effects on bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and mitochondrial function under oxidative stress conditions. The Ti-xCe (x=0-5 wt.%) gradient alloys were fabricated by vacuum arc melting, with subsequent microstructural characterization by metallographic analysis and mechanical property evaluation to determine the optimal cerium concentration. The selected composition was subjected to micro-arc oxidation (MAO) treatment (TiCeMAO group). Surface morphology was characterized by SEM. Antibacterial performance was systematically assessed. For biological evaluation, rBMSCs were cultured on material surfaces, where cell viability, cytotoxicity, and adhesion behavior were examined. Osteogenic differentiation capacity was quantified through qPCR, Western blot, ALP and alizarin red staining with quantitative analysis. The material's effects on mitochondrial function during oxidative stress were investigated by intracellular ROS detection, JC-1 assay, and quantification of electron transport chain complex expression. Ti-xCe (x=0-5 wt.%) alloys were successfully fabricated, with Ti-3Ce exhibiting optimal grain refinement and strength. TiCeMAO group demonstrated potent antibacterial effects, enhanced rBMSCs viability, extension and osteogenesis (P<0.01), and improved mitochondrial function as well as reduced ROS expression under oxidative stress (P<0.01). The TiCeMAO surface developed herein uniquely combines antibacterial activity, osteoinduction, and mitochondrial function modulation, offering a promising implant surface strategy for osteoporosis applications.

papers.title: Finite Element Analysis Of Biodegradable Materials For Mandibular Bone Defects
papers.abstract: To investigate the feasibility of applying various personalized biodegradable materials for bone graft fixation in mandibular RBS-type bone defects, and to provide biomechanical insights for the design of personalized biodegradable materials in mandibular defect reconstruction. Finite element models of personalized internal fixation systems combined with fibula reconstruction for mandibular RBS-type bone defects were established. Finite element simulations were performed on personalized biodegradable materials (zinc alloy, magnesium alloy, and polylactic acid) to analyze the feasibility of their application in internal fixation for mandibular RBS-type bone defects, with titanium alloy as a comparative control. Biomechanical changes were investigated by evaluating whether the maximum stress on fixation plates and screws exceeded the materials’ ultimate strength and identifying stress concentration areas within the fixation system. The maximum stress of magnesium alloy and polylactic acid was higher than their yield strength. The maximum equivalent stress of zinc alloy internal fixation reconstruction plate and screws was lower than their yield strength. Compared with the titanium alloy group, the zinc alloy group had lower equivalent stress and equivalent strain, more uniform stress distribution, and lower stress shielding of bone. The chin, mandibular angle turning point, and condyle were the stress concentration sites of the reconstruction plate. Finite element simulations demonstrated that the mechanical properties of biodegradable zinc alloy are sufficient for fixation in fibula-reconstructed mandibular RBS-type bone defects, although reinforcement at stress concentration areas of the reconstruction plate is required.

papers.title: Digital Implant Restoration In Edentulous Maxilla: 36-Month Follow-Up
papers.abstract: This case demonstrates a digitally assisted, prosthetically guided approach for implant-supported fixed rehabilitation in a patient with edentulous maxilla and severe alveolar bone atrophy. Stable outcomes were maintained throughout the 36-month follow-up. A 60-year-old female requiring implant-supported fixed maxillary rehabilitation. A transitional diagnostic denture was fabricated with DSD-based aesthetic analysis using 2D facial photographs. After 3 months, the denture served as a reference for definitive prosthetics. Final impressions, intraoral scans, and CBCT data were digitally merged to design surgical guides. Six implants were placed with bilateral sinus augmentation, ensuring even distribution and parallelism. After 6 months, intraoral scans with scan abutments captured implant positions and soft tissue contours, aligning with prior occlusal/prosthetic data to transfer transitional denture parameters to an implant-supported provisional prosthesis. Following 1 month of stable function and patient satisfaction, dynamic occlusal records (JMA electronic facebow) and digital scans guided definitive prosthesis. Follow-ups at 2 weeks, 3/6/12/24/36 months confirmed stable occlusion, intact prostheses, healthy peri-implant tissues, and successful osseointegration. This case used digital technology to transfer occlusal and aesthetic information step-by-step to the final prosthesis, achieving prosthetically guided implant design. Postoperative maintenance included oral hygiene education, and occlusal adjustments. At 36 months, implants and prostheses were stable Digital technology greatly improves the accuracy of implant restoration, achieving prosthetically guided precision implantation. Good oral hygiene maintenance and regular occlusal check-ups are necessary to ensure long-term stability of implant dentures.

papers.title: HERPUD1 Regulates T2DM Implant Angiogenesis-Osteogenesis By Accelerating TMBIM6 Ubiquitination
papers.abstract: This study aims to explore the regulatory mechanisms of H-type vessel-mediated angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupling in Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), focusing on the roles of HERPUD1 and TMBIM6 in endothelial progenitor cell (EPC) function under high glucose conditions. Under high glucose conditions, the expression levels of HERPUD1 and TMBIM6 were investigated in endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs). HERPUD1 knockdown (Herpud1 KD ) experiments were conducted to assess its impact on EPC function and H-type vessel expression. The regulatory relationship between HERPUD1 and TMBIM6, including ubiquitination and degradation processes, was examined. Rat models of T2DM were employed to evaluate the effects of Herpud1 KD on implant osseointegration. High glucose conditions significantly increased HERPUD1 expression in EPCs, impairing their function, while TMBIM6 levels decreased. Herpud1 KD rescued these impairments, promoting H-type vessel expression and improving implant osseointegration in T2DM rats. HERPUD1 was found to regulate TMBIM6 by accelerating its ubiquitination and degradation, thereby disrupting EPC angiogenesis and angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupling. The HERPUD1-TMBIM6-Ca 2+ axis plays a critical role in impairing EPC angiogenesis under high glucose conditions, affecting angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupling crucial for bone healing. Targeted therapies focusing on the ER pathway could potentially improve implant success rates in diabetic patients by enhancing H-type vessel function and osseointegration.

papers.title: Bone Column Technique For Narrow Alveolar Ridge Implant
papers.abstract: A 63-year-old female presented with missing right mandibular first premolar (tooth 44) due to caries extraction years prior. Clinical and CBCT evaluation revealed narrow alveolar ridge. The treatment plan included implant placement with simultaneous in-situ autogenous bone column augmentation. The patient’s medical history was unremarkable. Clinical examination revealed a knife-edged ridge (5 mm width, 11 mm height) with intact adjacent teeth (45, 47). CBCT confirmed insufficient buccal bone volume. Surgical steps included a crestal incision, harvesting a 3×7 mm autogenous bone column, and placing a implant (Astra EV 4.2×11 mm, 25 N stability). The bone column was fixed at the buccal concavity using a titanium screw (2.0×10 mm).Postoperative CBCT at 4 months demonstrated successful osseointegration and restored ridge contour. Final prosthesis delivery achieved healthy peri-implant tissues and functional occlusion. Traditional particulate graft materials demonstrate inferior mechanical properties that compromise their collapse resistance. The utilization of autologous bone columns as supportive structures effectively mitigates post-operative bone collapse. The in-situ bone column technique avoids secondary donor sites and achieves superior aesthetic results and long-term stability of the bone augmentation Combining bioactivity with mechanical stability, this technique offers an innovative approach for implant rehabilitation in edentulous areas with insufficient bone volume. It also combines functional rehabilitation with aesthetic preservation, offering a predictable alternative to GBR in complex cases.

papers.title: Novel Strategy For Iipp In Molar Region
papers.abstract: This strategy utilizes a surgical guide to precisely place tapered macro-threaded implants, achieving primary stability and enabling immediate loading. A 35-year-old female patient presented with a non-restorable right mandibular first molar. Clinical and radiographic evaluation revealed no acute infection and sufficient apical bone volume for primary stability. Following minimally invasive extraction, the placement of a Straumann BLX ® (Institute Straumann AG) achieved an insertion torque of 50Ncm. The jumping gap was filled with sticky bone graft and covered with a CGF membrane. Immediate postoperative digital intraoral scanning enabled the fabrication of a 3D-printed resin provisional crown, delivered the same day. After three months, the definitive prosthesis was fabricated by duplicating the provisional restoration parameters. Radiographic evaluation revealed no significant marginal bone resorption. Clinical evaluation revealed a peri-implant keratinized tissue width exceeding 3 mm, accompanied by a Jemt papilla index score of 2. To ensure the success of immediate loading, the provisional crown design was guided by electronic facebow to establish light occlusal contacts in maximum intercuspation. It also featured, anterior guidance for posterior disocclusion during protrusion and working-side canine guidance with non-working clearance in lateral excursions. Sticky bone graft demonstrates moldable morphology and ease of handling, enhancing hard tissue regeneration and maintaining marginal bone stability after immediate loading. The novel IIPP protocol in the molar region ensures primary stability, rapid occlusal recovery, and soft tissue preservation, while enhancing patient satisfaction by optimizing the treatment flow.

papers.title: Overexpression Of Aldh6a1 Rescues Osteoblasts And Facilitates Osseointegration In Hyperlipidemia
papers.abstract: Endogenous therapeutic targets for facilitating titanium implant osseointegration in hyperlipidemia remain elusive and this study aimed to elucidate the potential role of ALDH6A1 in osseointegration in hyperlipidemia mice. The animal experimental procedures were approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Stomatological Hospital, Shandong University, Jinan, China. Twenty-four 6-week-old male C57BL/6J mice were used to construct normal or hyperlipidemia femoral implant model, and overexpression of ALDH6A1 was achieved through local injection of lentivirus. Micro-CT and immunofluorescence staining were applied to detect osseointegration, oxidative damage, expression levels of ALDH6A1 in peri-implant tissue. In addition, primary osteoblasts from mouse skull were extracted and cultured for exploring the impact of changes in ALDH6A1 expression levels on the biological activity of osteoblasts. All data were presented as the mean ± standard deviation of at least three independent experiments. The P value less than 0.05 was considered to be statistically significant. In vivo, ALDH6A1 expression significantly decreased in hyperlipidemia mice, compared with normal mice (P < 0.05), and local overexpression of ALDH6A1 facilitated osseointegration in hyperlipidemia mice by reducing oxidative damage in peri-implant tissue. In vitro, ALDH6A1 was downregulated in high-fat environment and silencing ALDH6A1 led to osteogenic dysfunction. Additionally, ALDH6A1 overexpression reduced the fluorescence intensity of DCFH-DA and MitoSOX, and restored the expression of COLI, ALP, and RUNX2. Overexpression of ALDH6A1 significantly reshapes the biological activity of osteoblasts and improves osseointegration under hyperlipidemia. ALDH6A1 is a potential therapeutic target for hyperlipidemia related bone metabolism diseases.

papers.title: Preimplant Free Graft: 5-Year Peri-Implant Stability
papers.abstract: Insufficient attached gingiva (width <2 mm) is a critical risk factor for peri-implantitis due to plaque accumulation, mucosal recession, and compromised soft tissue stability. Preoperative soft tissue augmentation is essential for optimizing the peri-implant microenvironment in patients with thin gingival phenotypes. A 38-year-old female with inadequate keratinized gingiva (1 mm) at site 36 underwent pre-implant free gingival grafting (FGG). A partial-thickness flap was elevated, apically repositioned, and a palatal connective tissue graft sutured into the recipient bed. At 2 months post-FGG, keratinized width increased to 5 mm, enabling implant placement. Five-year follow-up revealed stable peri-implant probing depths (2–3 mm), 2 mm attached gingiva, and radiographically confirmed osseointegration without inflammation or bone loss. 1. Is soft tissue augmentation indicated for peri-implant keratinized gingiva deficiency? 2. Timing of soft tissue augmentation: Does pre-implant or pre-stage II surgery yield superior long-term stability? For thin phenotypes, the establishment of a keratinized zone of ≥2mm by FGG before implantation significantly reduced the risk of periimplantable inflammation within 5 years and enhanced soft tissue stability. This case provides a long-term clinical observation for preimplantation soft tissue reconstruction.

papers.title: Lipid Droplets Disturb Bone Homeostasis And Impair Osseointegration In Hyperlipidemia
papers.abstract: Hyperlipidemia impairs osseointegration and interferes the effect of implant restoration, and this study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanisms of lipid droplet accumulation induced by hyperlipidemia on disturbing bone homeostasis. The animal experimental procedures were approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Stomatological Hospital, Shandong University, Jinan, China. Twenty-four 6-week-old male C57BL/6J mice were used to construct normal or hyperlipidemia femoral implant model. Wnt3a or NAC were locally injected into the distal femur in hyperlipidemia mice for assessing changes of osseointegration, lipid droplet accumulation, and osteogenesis-osteoclasis balance by Micro-CT, hard tissue slicing and staining, H&E staining, TRAP staining, as well as immunofluorescence staining. Additionally, the relationship between lipid droplets and oxidative damage in BMMSCs cultured on titanium sheets surface were detected. In vivo, the osteogenesis-related ROS/Wnt/β-catenin pathway was downregulated and the osteoclasis-related ROS/RANKL/NF-κB pathway was upregulated in hyperlipidemia mice, compared with normal mice. In addition, local application of NAC could alleviate endoplasmic reticulum stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in situ, yet failed to reduce lipid droplet accumulation in peri-implant tissue. In vitro, the intracellular level of GSH/GSSG, MDA, ATP and the mean fluorescence intensity of BODIPY, GRP78, DCFH-DA in high-fat medium were significantly different with those in normal condition, and the effect of intermittent application of NAC was short-lived. Lipid droplet accumulation is the primary cause for inducing oxidative damage, disturbing osteogenesis-osteoclasis balance, and impairing osseointegration in hyperlipidemia.

papers.title: Digital Precision Workflow For Full-Arch Implant Rehabilitation
papers.abstract: Introduction This investigation establishes a customized implant prosthetic protocol for edentulous patients with heterogeneous clinical presentations based on a fully digitalized diagnostic and therapeutic system, aiming to achieve synergistically optimized outcomes in both functional rehabilitation and esthetic restoration. Case description This study establishes a multimodal data-integrated full-arch implant restoration system by synergizing oral implant fiducial markers, digital surgical guides, intraoral scanning, 3D facial scanning, and electronic facebow technologies. Utilizing fiducial markers to achieve high-precision spatial registration between jawbone imaging and intraoral scan data, the system constructs a three-dimensional virtual patient model incorporating anatomical structures, occlusal function, and aesthetic parameters through dynamic occlusal recordings and facial biometric integration. The surgical guides, fabricated via composite manufacturing processes, integrate navigation and occlusal positioning devices, significantly enhancing the precision of implant placement. This system enables precise implant placement, occlusal reconstruction, and aesthetic restoration. Discussion Comprehensive clinical follow-up and radiographic evaluations confirmed successful osseointegration in all patients postoperatively, with the establishment of stable occlusal relationships and attainment of anticipated aesthetic outcomes. Conclusion/clinical significance The system achieves full-process control from anatomical restoration, functional reconstruction to aesthetic rehabilitation through a technical closed-loop of "data acquisition - virtual planning - precise execution". Its core value lies in transforming traditional experience-dependent operations into data-driven precision medicine.

papers.title: Immediate Implantation Following Palatally Impacted Canine Extraction
papers.abstract: Introduction The management of impacted maxillary canines poses a significant challenge in diagnosis and treatment, often leading to lengthy and complex procedures. Historically, extraction followed by orthodontic alignment or prosthetic rehabilitation has been the go-to solution. However, the advent of dental implantology has opened up new avenues for immediate implantation in severely impacted or non-restorable canine sites. Case description A 31-year-old patient presented with a mobile deciduous canine and horizontally impacted upper right permanent canine, seeking a solution to maintain a fixed tooth without any period of edentulism. A multidisciplinary approach was adopted, involving the extraction of the lacteal canine, surgical removal of the impacted canine, immediate implant placement of a tapered dental implant followed by non-functional loading with a temporary crown to augment primary stability. Discussion The study aimed to investigate the feasibility of achieving primary stability in a reduced amount of bone through under-preparation of the osteotomy site. In a case where bone availability was limited, all visible palatal implant threads were grafted to enhance retention and fill the bone defect. The definitive prosthetic restoration was placed after 3 months. Digital periapical radiographs 9 months later, demonstrated peri-implant bone loss of 0.62 mm. Conclusion/clinical significance Immediate implantation in the impacted maxillary canine post-extraction site presents a promising approach to streamline treatment and optimize both functional and aesthetic outcomes. The technique may offer a viable alternative to traditional treatment methods, reducing the need for multiple interventions and improving patient satisfaction.

papers.title: Difference Between Classes Of Implants And Their Surface Contamination
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to differentiate the surface of high-end and low-end implants, i.e. which chemical elements are present on them during cleaning of the implants. One group (10 implants) consisted of high-end implants that have been extensively studied in scientific and clinical research and have been available on the market for a long time. The second group (10 implants) included newer implants that are relatively recent to the market, with limited research data available and a lower price point compared to the first group. The analysis focused on the surface of the dental implants and was conducted using a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM). The Electron Sample analysis can be performed using SE (Secondary Electron) and/or BSE (Backscattered Electron) detectors. With proper sample preparation, resolutions better than 5 nm can be achieved. Using scanning electron microscopy, a range of chemical elements was detected on the surfaces of implants across all study groups. The first group (low-end implants) showed a high presence of these elements. In contrast, the second group (high-end) of implants exhibited a notably different surface composition, containing only a minimal number of chemical elements. Titanium is the primary choice for implants due to its biocompatibility and durability, while the addition of elements such as calcium, phosphorus, zinc, magnesium, and silver can significantly enhance the process of osseointegration, increase stability, and reduce the risk of infections.

papers.title: Ai-Optimized 3D-Printed Abutments In Prosthodontics
papers.abstract: Aim or purpose To overcome the limitations of traditional abutments in biomechanical adaptation, this study integrates AI-driven biomechanical optimization and additive manufacturing to evaluate 3D-printed abutments' precision, stability, and biocompatibility. Materials and methods (1)AI Modeling: Finite element models from 128 CT scans predicted bone stress (>15 MPa threshold) from January 2023 to January 2025. Dynamic topology optimization refined abutment morphology (target: 30% stress reduction). (2)SLM Fabrication: Titanium abutments (Ti-6Al-4V ELI) were 3D-printed (SLM: 280W, 30μm layers) with HIP post-processing (100MPa, 920°C), achieving >99.9% density and Ra<2μm roughness. (3)Validation: Accuracy: Industrial CT (1μm) measured interface gaps; ISO 14801 fatigue testing (5×10⁶ cycles, 150N) assessed stability. Biocompatibility: Human gingival fibroblasts (CCK-8 assay) and porcine models (Micro-CT BV/TV) evaluated biological responses. Microbial Resistance: S. mutans biofilm assays quantified plaque adhesion. Results AI-optimized abutments reduced stress concentration by 48% (p<0.001) and exhibited superior mechanical performance (interface gaps: 18.3±2.4μm vs. 53.6±5.1μm, p<0.001; yield strength: 825±15MPa vs. 720±20MPa, p=0.001). Biological validation showed increased cell proliferation (27%, p=0.002) and enhanced osseointegration (BV/TV: 68.5±4.2% vs. 54.1±5.7%, p=0.008), while microbial adhesion decreased by 52% (p<0.01). Conclusions This AI-driven approach enhances precision, biomechanical stability, and biocompatibility of 3D-printed abutments, offering a transformative solution for complex prosthodontic rehabilitation.

papers.title: Sepu-Titanium Enhance Bone Regeneration In Metabolic Disorders Via Nrf2
papers.abstract: Titanium (Ti) implants, although widely used in clinical practice, still face challenges such as inflammation and impaired osseointegration, particularly in patients with metabolic disorders like diabetes and osteoporosis, who have higher risks of implant failure. Conventional Ti surface modification methods are limited by complex fabrication processes, poor adhesion strength, and the difficulty of simultaneously regulating immune responses and osteogenesis. In this study, we synthesized selenium-containing polyurethane (SePU) and functionalized Ti surfaces through a simple soaking method. At first, single-molecule force spectroscopy quantified the binding interactions between SePU and Ti. In addition, in vitro experiments assessed SePU’s effects on osteogenesis and macrophage polarization. Then, male SD rats, ZDF rats, and female OVX rats were respectively used to model healthy, diabetic, and osteoporotic conditions. SePU-modified Ti implants were placed in femurs of these rats to evaluate bone formation under different conditions via Micro-CT and histological analysis (Ethical approval: LA2023535). Moreover, RNA sequencing of peri-implant bone tissues explored potential mechanisms, which were further validated. Notably, SePU formed a chemical bond with Ti, induced M2 macrophage polarization, enhanced osteogenic differentiation, and promoted peri-implant bone formation in diabetic and osteoporotic rats. RNA sequencing and validation showed that SePU modulated NRF2-mediated oxidative stress by upregulating GSTM3. This enhanced ROS scavenging, reduced oxidative damage, thereby created an immune microenvironment conducive to regeneration. Our findings offer a novel strategy utilizing selenium to tackle the clinical challenges of Ti implants, especially for metabolic disorders like diabetes and osteoporosis that hinder osteogenesis.

papers.title: Gmsc-Apoevs Enhance Implant Osteointegration In Ovariectomy-Induced Osteoporotic Rats
papers.abstract: To investigate the therapeutic potential of apoptotic vesicles derived from gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSC-apoEVs) in enhancing implant osseointegration under estrogen-deficient conditions and elucidate the underlying mechanisms, thereby proposing a novel cell-free strategy for managing osteoporosis-related implant. Female SD rats (8-week-old) underwent ovariectomy (OVX) to model postmenopausal osteoporosis. Animals were allocated into sham, OVX and apoEV-treated groups. GMSC-apoEVs were administered intravenously per week post OVX, concurrent with titanium implants implanted in femurs at week 4. Bone morphology and osteointegration were assessed via micro-CT, histology assessment (H&E, Masson staining), and biomechanical testing at week 8. In vitro, the osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMMSCs) after GMSC-apoEVs treatment was evaluated using Alizarin Red S, ALP staining and Western blot. Proteomic analysis was used to further explore the molecular mechanisms. GMSC-apoEVs significantly enhanced bone-implant integration in OVX rats, evidenced by increased bone volume, trabecular thickness and biomechanical stability. GMSC-apoEVs restored osteogenic differentiation while decreasing adipogenic differentiation in OVX-BMMSCs. Proteomic analysis revealed GMSC-apoEVs rescued lysosomal dysfunction in OVX-BMMSCs, reactivating osteogenic pathways. GMSC-apoEVs transplantation enhances bone-implant integration in ovariectomized rats by rescuing osteogenic differentiation of BMMSCs via lysosome related pathway, offering a promising cell-free therapeutic approach for implant in estrogen-deficient conditions.

papers.title: Micro-Nano CFR-PEEK: Regulatory Code For Bone, Bacteria & Tube
papers.abstract: To address CFR-PEEK's limited clinical use due to inertness and poor osseointegration, this study constructs a Micro-Nano CFR-PEEK via sulfonation-nitration synergy, improving osseointegration, angiogenesis, anti-osteoclast and antibacterial properties, and reveal internal mechanisms to offer implant solutions. Dynamic monitoring technology was employed to quantitatively analyze the morphological changes of CFR-PEEK treated with mixed acids (sulfuric acid and nitric acid) in different proportions. The surface structure was optimized by regulating the synergistic effect of sulfonation and nitration. The osteogenic, angiogenic, osteoclast-inhibiting, and antibacterial properties of the treated materials were evaluated, and in-vivo experiments were conducted to verify the osseointegration effect. RNA sequencing analyzed osteogenic pathways and regulatory mechanisms of Micro-Nano modified CFR-PEEK. Dynamic mixed-acid treatment precisely constructed an ideal porous structure on the surface of CFR-PEEK. Uniformly distributed nanoparticles formed unexpectedly, significantly enhancing surface area and biological activity. The modified material not only showed excellent osteogenic, angiogenic, anti-osteoclast, and antibacterial abilities with in-vivo osseointegration improvement, but RNA sequencing also revealed activation of osteogenesis-related pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin. This study first constructs a CFR-PEEK surface composite with a porous structure and uniform nanoparticles via dynamic sulfonation-nitration synergy, breaking traditional corrosion-method limitations. The modified material optimizes triple functions: osseointegration, angiogenesis, and antibacterial activity. The overall achievement provides an innovative strategy for developing high-performance dental implant materials, bearing great clinical value.

papers.title: Zif-8(Cel)-Modified Peek Implant For Bone Regeneration
papers.abstract: The study aims to enhance bone regeneration using a ZIF-8(CEL)-modified PEEK implant for sustained bioactive release and osteoimmunomodulation. The study modified polyetheretherketone (PEEK) via sulfonation (SPEEK) to create a porous surface, followed by dopamine adhesion to immobilize ZIF-8 loaded with celecoxib (ZIF-8(CEL)), forming PEEK@ZIF-8(CEL). Material characterization included SEM, EDS, contact angle, and Zn²⁺/CEL release analysis (ICP-MS/HPLC). In vitro, MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts and RAW 264.7 macrophages were cultured to assess adhesion (SEM), viability (live/dead staining), osteogenic (BMP-6, Runx2) and inflammatory (TNF-α, IL-6) gene expression (RT-qPCR), and mineralization (SBF immersion). In vivo, PEEK@ZIF-8(CEL) was implanted into SD rat cranial defects. Bone regeneration was evaluated via micro-CT (BMD, BV/TV), histology (H&E, Goldner staining), immunohistofluorescence (Runx2, CD31), and nanoindentation for mechanical properties. Statistical analysis used ANOVA and t-tests (GraphPad Prism). Animal protocols were ethically approved. PEEK@ZIF-8(CEL) demonstrated enhanced osteogenic activity and anti-inflammatory effects through sustained release of Zn²⁺ and celecoxib. In vivo studies showed superior bone regeneration with higher bone density (BMD: 0.128 g/cm³) and volume (BV/TV: 72.2%) compared to unmodified PEEK. The material promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, improving osseointegration and mechanical strength in rat cranial defects. This study demonstrates the potential of PEEK@ZIF-8(CEL) as a novel repair material for large bone defects, offering a promising alternative in maxillofacial applications.

papers.title: Chronic Apical Periodontitis Implant Restoration With CTG: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Chronic apical periodontitis with bone defects elevates aesthetic risks in anterior implant rehabilitation. Flapless socket preservation preserves tissue dimensions when primary stability is unattainable, while connective tissue graft (CTG) establishes biological prerequisites for aesthetics. A 26-year-old female presented with a fractured maxillary left central incisor (#21) requiring implant restoration. Clinical findings included crown-root fracture with chronic apical periodontitis (#21), poor gingival contour, and inadequate root canal therapy (#11). Minimally invasive extraction of #21 was performed, followed by socket preservation using PRF membrane, low-resorption bone graft, and collagen sponge. At the 6-month postoperative evaluation, crown lengthening of tooth #11 was executed according to Digital Smile Design (DSD) principles to harmonize gingival contour, with simultaneous fabrication of a provisional restoration for #11 and an implant-supported interim prosthesis for #21. Once the transmucosal emergence profile of #21 was o. In localized chronic apical periodontitis, inflammatory granulation removal precedes socket preservation for bone defect rehabilitation. CTG induced predictable gingival biotype conversion, acting as a biomechanical foundation for peri-implant pink-white aesthetic. This case demonstrates that implant restoration combined with socket preservation and CTG in the esthetic zone with localized infectious lesions can achieve ideal esthetic outcomes.

papers.title: Clinical Application Of Locator Attachment In Mandibular Complete Denture Restoration
papers.abstract: The Locator attachment system for implant-supported overdentures combines endosseous implant technology with precision attachment mechanisms, offering a reliable solution for edentulous or partially edentulous patients. An 81-year-old female patient presented with a severely atrophic mandibular ridge and retained teeth 33, 34, 43 exhibiting Grade III mobility. After comprehensive evaluation, a mandibular implant-supported overdenture with Locator attachments was planned. After completing the examination, scheduled surgery can be performed. Under local anesthesia, teeth 33, 34, and 43 were extracted, and at the same time, two implants were implanted in teeth 33 and 43, along with bone powder and guided regeneration membrane. After 4 months, the CBCT showed good osseointegration around the implant, completing the second phase of repair. The advantages of using Locator attachment for implant supported dentures: 1.compared to traditional full dentures, locator attachments provide more durable and stable retention. 2. Surgical trauma is relatively minor. 3.Compared to planting fixed dentures, it is easier to restore a coordinated and stable occlusal relationship. 4.Denture maintenance can restore retention by replacing the gasket, with a low proportion of re lining. For edentulous patients with mandibular alveolar ridge atrophy, Locator attachment implant supported dentures are an excellent choice,which balances functionality and aesthetics and has a good restoration effect.

papers.title: Application Of Autologous Crown After Immediate Implantation: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Introduction This study evaluated the clinical efficacy of autologous crowns in immediate implantation for traumatic teeth. Case description A 32-year-old female underwent immediate implantation of a fractured left maxillary anterior tooth. The extracted tooth’s autologous crown, combined with resin filling, was polished and provisionally restored intraoperatively. At 6-month follow-up, the implant demonstrated successful osseointegration, stable peri-implant bone levels on imaging, and favorable gingival contour with preserved papilla height. Patient’satisfaction was high, and no significant soft-tissue recession was observed after final restoration. Discussion Immediate implantation with autologous crown restoration effectively maintains peri-implant soft-tissue architecture, particularly in aesthetic zones. Compared to temporary abutments, autologous crowns offer superior biocompatibility, minimize soft-tissue irritation, and preserve gingival morphology through their natural shape and adhesive retention, avoiding mechanical disruption during healing. This approach reduces treatment costs and eliminates the need for multiple abutment adjustments. Conclusion/clinical significance Autologous crowns serve as an optimal transitional restoration for immediate implantation in anterior regions, balancing aesthetics, biological compatibility, and cost-effectiveness. This method provides a promising clinical strategy for preserving peri-implant soft-tissue stability and enhancing patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: Report a case of immediate implantation of an maxillary central incisor after root fracture, with in vitro preparation of root fragment and replanting in the extraction socket to preserve the alveolar ridge. Five years after the surgery, the alveolar ridge was found to be preserved, the root slice could be seen on CBCT image, and the implant is maintaining osseointegration. The autologous root slice replantation technique broadens the clinical indications of the socket-shield technique. Its extraoral root preparation offers superior operability with direct visualization, significantly reducing technical demands on clinicians. The autologous root slice replantation technique can be used in cases of apical inflammation, fracture of the root under the bone margin, etc., which are inappropriate for the socket-shield technique, to preserve the alveolar bone volume, which is a simple and feasible method for clinical application.

papers.title: Mucograft For Wider Implant Keratinized Gingiva: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Numerous studies have shown that an adequately wide zone of keratinized gingiva is beneficial for the long - term stability of dental implants. Using collagen matrix (Geistlich Mucograft) for keratinized gingiva augmentation is a new surgical technique. A middle - aged female patient completed the implant placement of tooth 46 in our hospital 4 months ago. She came for a follow - up visit for keratinized gingiva augmentation. Examination revealed that the gingiva in the edentulous area of tooth 46 had healed well, with a keratinized gingiva width of only 1 - 2 mm. X - ray showed good osseointegration of the implant in tooth 46. We performed keratinized gingiva augmentation for the patient using Mucograft. The final restoration was completed 4 months later, and the newly formed keratinized gingival tissue was healthy and stable. Free gingival grafting is the standard procedure for keratinized gingiva augmentation, but it requires a second surgical site. Using Mucograft can simplify the procedure, reduce patient discomfort, and the color and texture of the regenerated area match and coordinate better with the surrounding tissues. Mucograft may be an ideal alternative to free gingival grafting.

papers.title: Research On Glucose-Sensitive Porous Tantalum Implants
papers.abstract: While dental implantation has become the standard treatment for tooth loss, its efficacy in diabetic patients remains limited due to impaired osseointegration and persistent inflammation. This study developed an innovative metabolically responsive drug delivery system on porous tantalum implants, utilizing aspirin's pharmacodynamic properties to achieve glucose-dependent release kinetics. 1. Fabricated a polydopamine-assisted mesoporous silica coating on porous tantalum implants for aspirin loading, with comprehensive characterization (SEM, EDS, Zeta potential) 2. In vitro evaluation: - Assessed osteogenic differentiation using ALP staining and Alizarin Red quantification - Analyzed osteogenic markers (ALP, RUNX-2, OPN) via immunofluorescence, qPCR, and Western blot - Evaluated macrophage polarization (iNOS, CD86, CD206) in RAW264.7 cell models 3. In vivo study: - Diabetic rat models were successfully established in 6-week-old male SD rats via streptozotocin (STZ) induction (Sigma, 35 mg/kg), with persistent hyperglycemia confirmed by fasting blood glucose measurements exceeding 16.7 mmol/L (Ethical approval number: YSY-DWLL-2024612). - Implanted modified porous tantalum in femoral bone - Evaluated osseointegration by micro-CT (BV/TV) and histological analysis at 8 and 12 weeks The modified implant surface demonstrated: - Glucose-responsive drug release properties - Enhanced osteogenic activity and bone matrix mineralization - Improved anti-inflammatory microenvironment The metabolic adaptive surface modification strategy developed in this study provides a new solution for implant functionalization in patients with diabetes and realizes the synergistic effect of drug release in response to blood glucose fluctuations and implant surface optimization.

papers.title: Transcrestal Sinus Floor Elevation With Robotic Force Feedback And Vision
papers.abstract: Osseodensification is a technique for transcrestal sinus floor elevation. It can densify bone and the water shock wave generated by drills can lift Schneiderian membrane. Autonomous dental implant robot is a newly computer-assisted implant system which combines the physical constraint of static guide and visualization of dynamic navigation, and has been widely used in clinic. A 24-year-old patient with upper left molar missing due to crown-root fracture 3months ago experienced insufficient residual bone height(RBH) and density. Autonomous dental implant robot (YaZhi, YakeRobot Technology Ltd) and osseodensification (Smart, Segma) kit were used for transcrestal sinus floor elevation(ADIR-OD-TSFE) and implantation. There was no membrane perforation, and the stability was excellent, with the angular error less than 2°. After 6months, CBCT revealed good osseointegration with 3-5mm height gain and 291.47mm³ volume augmentation. Preliminarily, ADIR-OD-TSFE is suitable for RBH≥3mm and no inflammation and tumor in maxillary sinus. Additionally, there are certain requirements for mouth opening. Membrane perforation is the most common complication in TSFE and related to membrane status, smoking, sinus floor septation, and intraoperative pressure. The visual and force feedback systems of ADIR provide the surgeon with "eyes" and "tactile sensation" during breakthrough process. And post-operative accuracy assessment showed its excellent control of depth, with the error of 0.29mm. This case presents a digital-guided surgery method using an ADIR for sinus floor elevation, osseodensification, and implantation in posterior maxillary tooth loss with low density and insufficient RBH.

papers.title: Digitally-Guided Implant Restoration In Aesthetic Zone With Embedded Teeth
papers.abstract: Implant surgery in the anterior aesthetic zone requires careful planning, especially for fully embedded teeth. Digital positioning guides with Guided Bone Regeneration (GBR) enhance implant precision and bone augmentation, offering a novel repair-oriented approach. The patient presented with a defect in the 11-22 region with severe ridge resorption and an embedded tooth in the apical region of 11. Initial treatment involving the fabrication of a diagnostic wax-up of resin teeth using the original removable denture as a reference. The patient wore the resin teeth for intraoral scanning after confirming satisfaction with morphology and occlusion. A digitally guided implant positioning system was designed with CBCT, using the restoration as a reference. Digitally guided implant placement with GBR was performed at sites 11 and 22. Six months later, second-stage surgery with gingival contouring and temporary restorations was completed, followed by the final restoration three months later. At the 1-year follow-up, the patient exhibited no discomfort. Imaging demonstrated successful osseointegration of the implants. CBCT and intraoral scanning technology acquire high-resolution 3D imaging data of the patient’s oral structures, which is integrated with implant planning software to optimize surgical precision, ensuring that the implant's position, angulation, and depth align with anatomical and functional requirements. For cases with bone-embedded teeth in the anterior aesthetic zone, the combination of digital surgical guides and CBCT can significantly reduce the complexity of the procedure.

papers.title: Dental Implants For Patients With Osteogenesis Imperfecta
papers.abstract: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), a rare disease caused by gene mutations, is accompanied with bone fragility, spontaneous fractures, and dental abnormalities and/or hypodontia. Among all phenotypes, patients with Type III/ IV variants are associated with the most severe symptoms. Implant treatment is often necessary to improve masticatory function. This study aimed to demonstrate the clinical outcomes of implant-supported restorations for these two OI patient types. Five patients, aged 26-44, suffered from tooth loss due to dentinogenesis imperfecta, caries and periodontitis. They had history of spontaneous fractures and previously undergone dental restorations that failed. Examination revealed oral complications such as alveolar malformation, low bone density, and dental diseases. Three of them had a history of bisphosphonate use. After comprehensive and multidisciplinary risk assessment, a personalized approach for each patient was adopted, with a total of 26 dental implants (n=2-15 each, AstraTech, Dentsply-Sirona). Clinical outcomes were monitored (T=6-30 months) with peri-implant bone stability demonstrated in all cases. OI affects multiple body systems, especially bones and teeth. Reports of implant treatment of OI patients were scarce, and the failure rate was high. In this study, functional stress distribution was optimized by patient-specific implant selection (size/number), prosthodontically-guided positioning, crown design and proper oral health maintenance, to ensure peri-implant bone stability. With multidisciplinary treatment model and standardized protocol, dental implants can achieve long-term stable reconstruction of masticatory function in patients with Type III/IV OI.

papers.abstract: Aim of study : The aim of the study was to compare between fabricated surgical guides and using roots of molar teeth as a guide in immediate implant placement in terms of Stability and Accuracy. Patients and Methods: A prospective clinical study was used in this investigation. 20 patients were divided into two groups: 10 immediate implants were inserted in group (A) study group using interradicular bone drilling between roots of molar teeth, and 10 immediate implants were placed in group (B) using prefabricated surgical guide, CBCT done immediately postoperative to evaluate implant accuracy, Osstell was utilized to ascertain the intraoperative primary stability and secondary stability six months later. Results: 18 implants were successfully functioning in both groups (A,B), For implant accuracy, there was no statistical significance between two groups (A,B) . Also for the implant stability, there was no statistical significance between two groups (A,B). Conclusions: Interradicular bone drilling teqnique increases implant position accuracy, stability, and operation feasibility very similar to prefabricated surgical guide, which demonstrated only slight increase in Stability and Accuracy. keywords: Immediate implant placement, intraradicular drilling technique, conventional. fabricated surgical guides.Running title: Various methods for immediate posterior mandibular implants.

papers.title: Heterotopic Ossification in Cementless Trochanteric Sparing Short Stem Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background: Heterotopic ossification (HO) is a common complication of total hip arthroplasty (THA), which can adversely affect patient satisfaction. Although the direct anterior approach (DAA) has been associated with lower rates of HO, the exact clinical impact of even low-grade ossification following DAA THA remains underreported. We aimed to assess the clinical impact of HO in DAA THA and identify demographics and implant-related risk factors. Methods: A retrospective single-center cohort study of 348 hips treated via DAA THA with a cementless short stem between January 2011 and December 2021 was performed. HO was graded at ≥12 months using the Brooker classification on standardized anteroposterior radiographs. The Harris Hip Score (HHS), the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC), and the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) were assessed at a mean of 4.3 years of follow-up. Comparative analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify independent predictors of HO. Results: HO occurred in 18.1% of hips: Brooker grade I in 12.4%, II in 3.0%, and III in 3.0%; no grade IV lesions developed. At final follow-up, patients without HO had significantly better outcomes compared with those with HO (all p < 0.001). When stratified by severity, even low-grade HO (Brooker I-II) was associated with significantly worse WOMAC (p = 0.023) and HHS (p < 0.001) compared with the non-HO group. Although VAS pain was higher in the low-grade group, the difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.084). On multivariable analysis, independent implant-related risk factors included use of the Continuum acetabular cup (odds ratio [OR] 2.10; p = 0.014), each additional millimeter of cup diameter (OR 1.16; p = 0.003), and longer femoral neck length (OR 2.06; p = 0.006). Conclusions: HO was observed in nearly one-fifth of hips, and even low-grade ossification was associated with significantly worse mid-term functional outcomes. Cup design, size, and neck length were identified as significant, modifiable predictors of HO risk. Careful implant selection may help reduce the incidence of HO and enhance postoperative function. Level of Evidence: Therapeutic Level II. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

papers.title: Femoral Neck System and Cannulated Compression Screws in the Treatment of Femoral Neck Fractures
papers.abstract: Introduction Femoral neck fractures (FNF) pose a significant risk for the elderly, with a 1-year mortality rate ranging from 20.6% to 25.4%, and nearly 50% of survivors facing long-term functional decline1,2. Displaced, unstable femoral neck fractures in older adults are usually an indication for early surgical intervention, which includes hemiarthroplasty or total hip replacement3. Other treatment methods typically involve osteosynthesis techniques such as dynamic hip screws (DHS), multiple cannulated screws, and femoral neck system (FNS), all designed to achieve stable fixation4. However, surgical failure and reoperation rates can vary between 8% and 21%, underscoring the need for more effective treatment options to improve patient outcomes5. The FNS is an innovative implant that aims to overcome the limitations of traditional fixation methods6. It seeks to reduce complications such as implant cutout, femoral neck shortening, and varus collapse, particularly in elderly patients and those with osteoporosis7. Biomechanical studies suggest that the FNS provides enhanced rotational stability and features a compact design, which minimizes soft tissue irritation and increases patient comfort8–10. Nonetheless, concerns regarding its long-term effectiveness and potential complications, including specific patterns of periprosthetic fractures, persist11,12. Internal fixation using cannulated compression screws (CCS) represents a minimally invasive approach that preserves the natural anatomy of the hip joint and facilitates early rehabilitation. This method can help reduce the need for hip replacement and associated complications13. However, CCS offers limited fracture stability and is linked to high rates of implant removal14,15. Among cases with complications, the most common were nonunion (39.2%), avascular necrosis (31.9%), reoperations (15.2%), and conversion to total hip arthroplasty (12.4%)16. Given the increased mortality, risk of disability, and likelihood of subsequent surgeries associated with femoral neck fractures, selecting the appropriate osteosynthesis method is crucial. Although several meta-analyses have evaluated the clinical performance of the FNS and CCS, their conclusions are sometimes inconsistent and vary in terms of methodological quality, included studies, and reported outcomes. Furthermore, no single study has comprehensively compared or synthesized the findings across these multiple meta-analyses. In addition, the higher cost of the FNS compared with CCS represents an important consideration in implant selection, potentially influencing clinical decision making and accessibility. Therefore, an umbrella review—by integrating data from existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses—offers a higher-level evidence synthesis to determine the relative effectiveness and safety of FNS versus CCS. The aim of this umbrella review was to evaluate and compare the clinical performance of the FNS and CCS in treating femoral neck fractures, focusing on key outcomes such as operation time, intraoperative blood loss, fluoroscopy frequency, hospital stay duration, fracture healing time, postoperative weight-bearing time, HHS, Barthel Index, total complications, nonunion rates, AVN, fixation failure, and femoral neck shortening. Methods This umbrella review followed the guidelines set forth by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)17. The study was prospectively registered at PROSPERO (CRD42024579646) on August 27, 2024. Search Strategy Relevant studies were identified through a search of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and Web of Science from January 2002 to August 1, 2024. The search query included the terms: ((“femur neck”[MeSH Terms] OR (“femur”[All Fields] AND “neck”[All Fields]) OR “femur neck”[All Fields] OR (“femoral”[All Fields] AND “neck”[All Fields]) OR “femoral neck”[All Fields]) AND (“system”[All Fields] OR “system s”[All Fields] OR “systems”[All Fields])) AND (meta-analysis[Filter] OR systematic review[Filter]). The search strategy for this review followed the method validated by Aromataris et al.18, including only English-language studies. COVIDENCE software was used to manage references, screen studies, extract data, and generate reports for the umbrella review. Eligibility Criteria The PICO-D (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, and Design) criteria (Table I) were used by 2 authors to independently screen titles and abstracts and identify eligible meta-analyses, with disagreements resolved by a third author to reach consensus. Only studies reporting accurate data on FNS versus CCS in femoral neck fractures were included and imported into COVIDENCE for screening, data extraction, and report generation. TABLE I - Eligibility Criteria for Studies on Femoral Neck System and Cannulated Compression Screws in the Treatment of Femoral Neck Fractures (PICO-D) Component Inclusion Criteria Exclusion Criteria Population (P) Adults with various types of femoral neck fractures undergoing surgical treatment Pediatric patients, pathological fractures, nonsurgical management, multiple trauma cases Intervention (I) Use of the FNS Studies not focused on FNS or combining FNS with other techniques without clear outcome differentiation Comparison (C) Use of CCS Studies not comparing FNS with CCS or involving other surgical techniques Outcomes (O) Clinical outcomes such as operation time, intraoperative blood loss, fluoroscopy frequency, hospital stay, weight-bearing time, healing time, Harris-Hip Score (HHS), Barthel Index, total complications, nonunion rates, avascular necrosis (AVN), fixation failure, femoral neck shortening, and postoperative weight-bearing time Studies that do not report on the specified outcomes, have insufficient statistical data, or do not provide confidence intervals and p-values Design (D) Systematic review or meta-analyses Non-comparative studies, case reports, and biomechanical studies without human subjects were excluded. In addition, meta-analyses with overlapping primary studies were excluded to avoid duplication of data and ensure the independence of findings CCS = cannulated compression screws, and FNS = femoral neck system. Data Extraction and Synthesis Two authors conducted a thorough review of the full text and independently extracted data. To minimize potential bias from overlapping data, all included meta-analyses were screened for duplicate primary studies during the full-text review, and any meta-analyses with overlapping studies were excluded from the analysis. The report summarizes the characteristics and findings of the included meta-analyses. Extracted data included author, year, data sources, sample size, group distribution, demographics, and outcomes. Categorical variables were reported as odds ratio (OR), risk ratio (RR), risk difference (RD) with 95% confidence interval (CI), and continuous variables as MD with 95% CI and p-values. Heterogeneity was assessed with I2. Methodological Quality Evaluation The methodological quality of included meta-analyses was evaluated with the AMSTAR 2 tool by 2 independent authors, while a third reviewer resolved any disagreements. This 16-item instrument rates responses as “Yes,” “No,” “Partially Yes,” or “Not Applicable” and classifies review quality as high, moderate, low, or critically low according to the number and severity of weaknesses19. Results General Characteristics The literature search (Fig. 1) identified 252 records. After removing 23 duplicates, 229 records were screened, leading to the assessment of 79 full texts. Eight meta-analyses published between 2022 and 2023 met the inclusion criteria20–27, comprising 6 to 21 studies each, with a total of 5,682 participants (Table II).Fig. 1: Flow diagram of the study selection process according to the PRISMA guidelines. Intraoperative and Postoperative Outcomes Blood Loss Eight meta-analyses (3,526 patients) examined blood loss (Appendix 1) after FNS and CCS surgery20–27. The CCS group consistently had significantly lower intraoperative blood loss, with mean differences ranging from 14.72 to 23.72 mL (p < 0.05). Number of Intraoperative Fluoroscopy Exposures The number of intraoperative fluoroscopy exposures (Appendix 1) was evaluated in 5 meta-analyses (2,010 patients)21–23,26,27. The FNS group consistently required fewer fluoroscopy exposures than the CCS group. Mean differences ranged from −8.19 to −11.46 (p < 0.05). Recorded operation time Seven studies (4,623 participants) assessed operative time (Appendix 1)20–27. Five meta-analyses with 3,455 patients found no significant difference (WMD: −7.96 to 6.65 min)21,23–25,27. However, 2 studies reported a significantly longer operative time in the CCS group20,22. Hospital stays Four meta-analyses (795 participants) found no significant difference in hospital stay duration between the FNS and CCS groups (Appendix 1)20–23. Fracture healing time Eight meta-analyses (3,727 participants) assessed fracture healing time (Appendix 1)20–27. Seven meta-analyses (3,416 patients) showed significantly shorter healing times in the FNS group (WMD/SMD: −0.75 to −1.54, p < 0.05)20,22–29. However, 1 study found no significant difference (p = 0.11)21. Weight-bearing time Two meta-analyses (436 participants) found FNS significantly reduced time to weight-bearing compared with CCS (MD: −4.10 days, p < 0.00001; SMD: −1.08, p = 0.04) (Appendix 1)21,26. Complications Delayed Union or Nonunion Four meta-analyses (2,037 participants) assessed delayed union or nonunion (Appendix 1)21,23,24,27. Two studies reported no significant difference21,23, while Wu et al.24 and Zhou et al.27 found that the FNS group had a significantly lower incidence of delayed union or nonunion compared with the CCS group. Femoral Neck Shortening Seven meta-analyses (3,060 participants) assessed the outcome of femoral neck shortening (Appendix 1)20,21,23–27. Six meta-analyses reported significantly less shortening with FNS (p < 0.05)21,23–27, while Gupta et al. found no significant difference20. Fixation Failure Five meta-analyses (3,202 participants) assessed fixation failure or cutout (Appendix 1)21,23,24,26,27. Three analyses found a significantly lower implant failure rate in the FNS group (p < 0.05)23,26,27, while 2 studies reported no significant difference between FNS and CCS21,24. AVN Five meta-analyses (3,213 participants) assessed avascular necrosis (AVN) (Appendix 1)21,23,24,26,27. Three analyses found a significantly lower AVN rate in the FNS group (p < 0.05)23,26,27, while 2 studies reported no significant difference21,24. Total Complications Five meta-analyses (2,544 participants)21,23,25,27 assessed the occurrence of total complications (Appendix 1). All analyses showed a significantly lower incidence of total complications with FNS compared with CCS (p < 0.05). Functional Outcomes HHS A total of 8 meta-analyses (4,457 patients) evaluated the Harris-Hip Score (HHS) (Appendix 1)20–27. All meta-analyses indicated that the FNS group had significantly higher HHS compared with the CCS group. The range of MD was 3.31 to 21.27 (p < 0.05). Barthel Index One meta-analysis (193 patients) assessed the Barthel Index (Appendix 1)27. The FNS group showed significantly greater improvement in basic activities of daily living than the CCS group (MD: 4.31, p < 0.05). Methodological Quality Evaluation Quality assessment showed that 5 meta-analyses (62.5%) were “critically low”20–22,24,27, and 3 (37.5%) were “low” quality,23,25,27 with none rated as “moderate” or “high quality” (Table III). Common issues included missing lists of excluded studies (5/8), unassessed funding sources (3/8), and lack of protocol registration (6/8). papers.title: Radiographic Aids in Dental Implantology – A Review
papers.abstract: Radiographic imaging is crucial in dental implantology for preoperative evaluation, precise surgery, and postoperative monitoring. While traditional methods such as Orthopantomogram (OPG) and intraoral periapical radiographs (IOPA) offer initial assessments, cone-beam computed tomography has emerged as the gold standard because of its three-dimensional precision. Complex cases that call for soft-tissue examination benefit from the use of advanced modalities such as computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging. Real-time navigation systems, 3D-printed surgical guides, and guided implant surgery are examples of radiographic aids that improve implant placement accuracy and lower complications. For the purpose of tracking osseointegration and identifying implant-related issues such as peri-implantitis and implant failure, postoperative imaging is essential. Future developments in low-dose imaging, augmented reality-based planning, and artificial intelligence (AI) will enhance digital workflows, radiation safety, and diagnostic accuracy. Implant success rates and patient outcomes will be significantly improved as technology advances by incorporating AI-assisted diagnostics, virtual planning, and real-time imaging.

papers.title: Chitosan-based Materials in Dental Implantology: A Review Article on Their Potential and Applications
papers.abstract: The biocompatibility, biodegradability, and prospective therapeutic applications of chitosan (CS), a biopolymer derived from chitin, have sparked attention in the field of dental implantology. This review examines various CS-based polymers and their use in dental implants, focusing on how they enhance osseointegration, reduce infection risk, and raise overall implant success rates. The study also covers the latest developments, difficulties, and potential paths for CS integration in dental implant materials.
